title: Automatically Selecting Answer Templates to Respond to Customer Emails
abstract: Studies authentic customer-support email in which an incoming message can contain several questions and agents compose replies from one or more answer templates. The method identifies portions of customer queries requiring responses and learns associations between actual questions and answers from query-response email pairs, with evaluation including real contact-center data.
venue: Proceedings of the 20th International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI 2007)

title: Characterizing and Supporting Question Answering in Human-to-Human Communication
abstract: Empirically studies question answering in a large enterprise-email collection and supplements the corpus analysis with a user survey. It defines extraction of question-answer pairs from threaded email conversations and evaluates neural question-to-answer matching at multiple granularities on manually labeled email data.
venue: The 41st International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research & Development in Information Retrieval

title: Online shopping customer service dialogue annotation and analysis
abstract: Builds an empirical corpus from real online-shopping customer-service dialogues and manually analyzes question relevance and question-answer matching. The study reports substantial cross-matching and implicit matching between questions and answers, making it relevant to nonlocal response alignment.
venue: Journal of Shandong University (Natural Science)

title: Multi-unit questions in institutional interactions: Sequential organizations and communicative functions
abstract: Analyzes a corpus of roughly four hundred multi-unit questions from authentic institutional interactions including health care, court trials, police interrogations, and social-welfare encounters. It identifies sequential organizations involving multiple interrogative and declarative units and examines how the units jointly constrain subsequent responses.
venue: Text

title: Answers to Japanese Multi-unit Questions with Explicit Assumptions
abstract: Uses conversation analysis on Japanese interview dialogues containing multi-unit questions. It specifically examines how respondents organize answers so as to respond to individual units of a multi-unit question and how they resist assumptions encoded in particular units.
venue: JELS 31

title: Asking more than one question in one turn in oral examinations and its impact on examination quality
abstract: Analyzes authentic video-recorded Norwegian oral examinations containing multi-unit questions. The study explicitly asks whether candidates respond to all questions or only some of them and finds that, when questions are separated by intervening talk, respondents often address only the final question.
venue: Journal of Pragmatics

title: Student-initiated multi-unit questions in EMI classrooms
abstract: Conversation-analytic study based on thirty hours of videotaped teacher-education classroom interaction. It examines how students construct multi-unit questions and how the combination of units narrows and structures the scope of the information sought in the ensuing interaction.
venue: Linguistics and Education

title: Reformulation of questions with candidate answers
abstract: Studies a multi-unit format in which an open question is reformulated as a more specific yes-no question or a set of alternatives. The reformulation supplies candidate answers and changes the response space against which the recipient's subsequent answer is interpreted.
venue: International Journal of Bilingualism

title: A coding scheme for question–response sequences in conversation
abstract: Presents the empirical coding scheme used in a ten-language comparative project on naturally occurring question-response sequences. The response annotation distinguishes answers, non-answer responses, and absence of a response, and separately records confirmation versus disconfirmation for polar questions.
venue: Journal of Pragmatics

title: An overview of the question–response system in American English conversation
abstract: Analyzes hundreds of questions from videotaped spontaneous American English conversations. It characterizes question types, social actions, and response types, providing empirical evidence about how natural responses satisfy or fail to fit prior questions.
venue: Journal of Pragmatics

title: Transformative answers: One way to resist a question’s constraints
abstract: Empirically analyzes transformative answers, in which a recipient answers while retroactively modifying either terms in the question or the agenda established by the question. The study provides fine-grained evidence that response scope and answerhood cannot always be modeled as simple acceptance of the question as originally posed.
venue: Language in Society

title: Non-Sentential Utterances in Dialogue: A: Corpus-Based Study
abstract: Presents a corpus-based study of non-sentential utterances in dialogue, including short answers and other fragments whose interpretation depends on prior conversational material. The analysis motivates explicit recovery of the contextual antecedent needed to interpret such responses.
venue: Proceedings of the Third SIGdial Workshop on Discourse and Dialogue

title: Towards Finding and Fixing Fragments—Using ML to Identify Non-Sentential Utterances and their Antecedents in Multi-Party Dialogue
abstract: Uses machine learning to identify fragmentary non-sentential utterances in multi-party dialogue and to determine their antecedents. Because fragments include context-dependent responses, the task directly requires choosing which previous conversational material supplies their interpretation.
venue: Proceedings of the 43rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Scaling up from Dialogue to Multilogue: Some Principles and Benchmarks
abstract: Examines how dialogue interpretation mechanisms scale to conversations with more than two participants. Corpus evidence on non-sentential utterances is used to study contextual resolution, including cases where the relevant antecedent is not simply the immediately preceding contribution.
venue: Proceedings of the 43rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Coding Dialogs with the DAMSL Annotation Scheme
abstract: Describes the DAMSL dialogue-act annotation scheme and reports initial human-annotation reliability. Its backward communicative functions explicitly encode how a current utterance relates to earlier dialogue, including answering a question, accepting a proposal, and confirming understanding, while allowing multiple communicative functions on an utterance.
venue: Working Notes of the AAAI Fall Symposium on Communicative Action in Humans and Machines

title: The DialogBank: dialogues with interoperable annotations
abstract: Introduces a collection of dialogues with gold-standard ISO 24617-2 annotations, including reannotations of existing corpora. The standard's multidimensional dialogue-act representation and functional dependencies provide structured evidence for response acts whose interpretation depends on earlier dialogue acts.
venue: Language Resources and Evaluation

title: Discourse Structure and Dialogue Acts in Multiparty Dialogue: the STAC Corpus
abstract: Introduces an SDRT-annotated corpus of multi-party chat with full discourse structures rather than isolated relation labels. Its graph annotations represent explicit links between elementary discourse units in interleaved conversational threads and support response relations such as question-answer, acknowledgement, clarification, and strategic acceptance or rejection.
venue: Proceedings of the Tenth International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC'16)

title: Modelling Structures for Situated Discourse
abstract: Studies complete SDRT structures in situated multi-party chat and analyzes interactions among linguistic moves, nonlinguistic events, discourse threads, and higher-order structures. The work is relevant to responses whose discourse target is a complex discourse unit rather than a single preceding utterance.
venue: Dialogue & Discourse

title: Discourse Structure for the Minecraft Corpus
abstract: Introduces the Minecraft Structured Dialogue Corpus with complete situated SDRT discourse structures over human collaborative dialogue and actions. The accompanying parser predicts discourse attachments and relation labels, including challenging long-distance attachments.
venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Joint International Conference on Computational Linguistics, Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC-COLING 2024)

title: A Deep Sequential Model for Discourse Parsing on Multi-Party Dialogues
abstract: Presents a sequential discourse parser for multi-party dialogue. For each elementary discourse unit, the model selects a previous EDU as its antecedent and predicts the corresponding discourse relation, jointly constructing a dialogue dependency structure.
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

title: A Structure Self-Aware Model for Discourse Parsing on Multi-Party Dialogues
abstract: Predicts discourse dependency structures for multi-party dialogues by modeling candidate EDU-to-EDU edges jointly rather than relying only on previous incremental decisions. Evaluation is performed on conversational discourse-parsing benchmarks where antecedent attachment and relation type must both be recovered.
venue: Proceedings of the Thirtieth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence

title: Improving Multi-Party Dialogue Discourse Parsing via Domain Integration
abstract: Studies prediction of discourse dependency structure and relations between elementary discourse units in multi-party dialogue. It evaluates cross-domain attachment and relation prediction and develops domain-integration methods for transferring dialogue discourse parsers across conversational settings.
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd Workshop on Computational Approaches to Discourse

title: Structured Dialogue Discourse Parsing
abstract: Jointly predicts discourse links and corresponding relation types in multi-participant conversations. Structured encoding and decoding produce a labeled multi-root non-projective discourse structure, allowing nonlocal response dependencies rather than assuming simple adjacency.
venue: Proceedings of the 23rd Annual Meeting of the Special Interest Group on Discourse and Dialogue

title: Speaker-Aware Discourse Parsing on Multi-Party Dialogues
abstract: Presents a speaker-aware parser for discourse dependency structures in multi-party dialogue. The model exploits interactions among speakers while predicting which earlier discourse unit a current unit attaches to and the relation associated with that attachment.
venue: Proceedings of the 29th International Conference on Computational Linguistics

title: A speaker-aware multiparty dialogue discourse parser with heterogeneous graph neural network
abstract: Models dialogue utterances and speakers in a heterogeneous graph and predicts both discourse dependency links and relation types. Experiments use the STAC and Molweni multi-party dialogue benchmarks, so the task requires selecting response antecedents rather than classifying relations for gold pairs.
venue: Cognitive Systems Research

title: Improving Dialogue Discourse Parsing via Reply-to Structures of Addressee Recognition
abstract: Combines dialogue discourse parsing with reply-to information derived from addressee recognition. The model uses reply-to structure as auxiliary evidence for predicting discourse links and relation types on STAC and Molweni.
venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: Hierarchical graph fusion network and a new argumentative dataset for multiparty dialogue discourse parsing
abstract: Introduces new annotated argumentative multi-party dialogue datasets together with a graph-based discourse parser. The task extracts relationships between elementary discourse units in complex conversations, requiring attachment selection and relation prediction rather than only utterance-level dialogue-act classification.
venue: Information Processing & Management

title: Discourse Relation Prediction and Discourse Parsing in Dialogues with Minimal Supervision
abstract: Develops a semi-supervised pipeline that first predicts dialogue discourse structures and then discourse relations. Evaluation includes STAC and cross-domain technical chat, providing evidence about antecedent attachment in a conversational domain beyond game chat.
venue: Proceedings of the 5th Workshop on Computational Approaches to Discourse (CODI 2024)

title: Enhancing Multi-party Dialogue Discourse Parsing with Explanation Generation
abstract: Augments multi-party dialogue discourse parsing with LLM-generated explanatory and contrastive information. It evaluates structural parsing on STAC and Molweni, where systems must recover discourse attachments and relation types among conversational units.
venue: Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Computational Linguistics

title: End-to-end dialogue structure parsing on multi-floor dialogue based on multi-task learning
abstract: Empirically studies dialogue structure in multi-floor collaborative robot-navigation conversations, where several concurrent conversational transactions may be active. The parser predicts antecedent links for utterances and then relation types, with dialogue-response prediction used as an auxiliary task.
venue: Frontiers in Robotics and AI

title: Integer Linear Programming for Discourse Parsing
abstract: Uses integer linear programming to perform global discourse parsing rather than independent pair classification. The formulation is applicable to graph-structured multi-party dialogue and supports attachment structures that are not restricted to a simple local tree, making it relevant to complex and potentially multi-parent discourse organization.
venue: Proceedings of the 2016 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies

title: Weak Supervision for Learning Discourse Structure
abstract: Evaluates weak-supervision strategies for learning discourse structure in multi-party dialogue. The experiments address discourse attachment rather than only relation classification, so the system must identify which earlier discourse unit a later contribution is linked to.
venue: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and the 9th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing

title: Anaphoric Annotation in the ARRAU Corpus
abstract: Introduces an anaphorically annotated corpus that explicitly represents multiple antecedents for ambiguous anaphoric expressions and discourse antecedents for references to abstract entities such as events, actions, and plans. The corpus includes task-oriented TRAINS dialogues, making its annotation model directly reusable for ambiguous or multi-unit non-nominal antecedents in dialogue.
venue: Proceedings of the Sixth International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC'08)

title: Anaphora Resolution with the ARRAU Corpus
abstract: Defines benchmark datasets and evaluation procedures from ARRAU for identity anaphora, bridging, and discourse deixis. The discourse-deixis task requires resolving references to abstract discourse content rather than only nominal entities, and ARRAU includes dialogue material.
venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Computational Models of Reference, Anaphora and Coreference

title: Anaphora Resolution in Dialogue: Description of the DFKI-TalkingRobots System for the CODI-CRAC 2021 Shared-Task
abstract: Describes an anaphora-resolution system for dialogue whose discourse-deixis component detects discourse-anaphor and antecedent pairs. This component directly models links from referring expressions to prior discourse content rather than only entity coreference.
venue: Proceedings of the CODI-CRAC 2021 Shared Task on Anaphora, Bridging, and Discourse Deixis in Dialogue

title: The CODI-CRAC 2022 Shared Task on Anaphora, Bridging, and Discourse Deixis in Dialogue
abstract: Describes conversational datasets and evaluation tasks for identity, bridging, and discourse deixis in dialogue. Its discourse-deixis annotations and evaluation are relevant to selecting antecedent discourse content that is propositional or otherwise non-nominal.
venue: Proceedings of the CODI-CRAC 2022 Shared Task on Anaphora, Bridging, and Discourse Deixis in Dialogue

title: Getting at Discourse Referents
abstract: Uses conversational data to compare discourse-anaphoric uses of the pronoun it with demonstrative that. The empirical analysis examines how grammatical and attentional properties of earlier discourse determine which discourse referent is selected.
venue: 27th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Some Facts About Centers, Indexicals, and Demonstratives
abstract: Empirically examines demonstrative and personal-pronoun reference in discourse. It shows that demonstratives can access discourse entities that are not the current local center, supporting antecedent-selection mechanisms that are not restricted to the immediately salient nominal referent.
venue: 29th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Abstract Pronominal Anaphora in Three Registers of English
abstract: Compares abstract pronominal anaphora across newswire, spontaneous dialogue, and planned speech. The corpus annotation explicitly marks non-nominal antecedents of it, this, and that when they refer to events, facts, propositions, or other abstract discourse entities.
venue: PSU McNair Scholars Online Journal

title: Annotation guidelines for Questions under Discussion and information structure
abstract: Presents a meaning-based annotation method for Questions under Discussion in naturally attested written and spoken data. The framework decomposes discourse according to the questions individual assertions answer and is designed to represent information-structural relations including answers that address only part of an active question.
venue: Information Structure in Lesser-described Languages: Studies in prosody and syntax

title: Discourse Deixis: Reference to Discourse Segments
abstract: Develops a computational account of discourse-deictic expressions that refer through prior discourse segments rather than ordinary nominal entities. The work establishes discourse segments as selectable antecedent units from which abstract discourse referents can be derived.
venue: 26th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Structure and Ostension in the Interpretation of Discourse Deixis
abstract: Examines demonstrative pronouns whose interpretation refers to the meaning of one or more clauses. It distinguishes the discourse segment that a demonstrative points to from the abstract entity obtained through that pointing, providing a mechanism for antecedents composed from larger stretches of discourse.
venue: Language and Cognitive Processes

title: A simplest systematics for the organization of turn-taking for conversation
abstract: Develops and empirically motivates a model of turn-taking from naturally occurring conversation. Although it does not provide proposition-level computational annotations, its concepts of next-speaker selection, transition relevance, and recipient design are foundational for later empirical work on sequential response relations.
venue: Language

title: Remarks on this and that
venue: Papers from the Tenth Regional Meeting of the Chicago Linguistic Society
